overview.description: Marriage Rummy (also known simply as Marriage) is a complex Rummy-style game popular in Nepal, Bhutan, and parts of Northern India. Played with three standard 52-card decks, each player receives 21 cards. The game features a unique 'Wild Card' system (Tiplu, Poplu, Jhiplu) and requires players to form three initial pure sets before they can 'see the joker' and use wild cards.
overview.deck: 156 cards (Three standard 52-card decks, no jokers printed)

history.origins: Originating in the Himalayas (Nepal), the game evolved from standard Rummy to accommodate more players and deeper strategic complexity through the use of three decks.
timeline: 1950s: Modern Rummy variants become popular in Kathmandu
1980s: The '21-card' ruleset with the Tiplu/Poplu/Jhiplu system stabilizes
Present: The national card game of Nepal, found in almost every social club and household
2010s: Popular mobile app genre in the South Asian market
Festivals: Widely played during Dashain and Tihar festivals
history.evolution: The 3-deck system and the 'Marriage' (three identical jokers) create massive point payouts that define the game's high-stakes nature. The wild card system is unique to this regional variant.
history.cultural: Commonly played during Dashain (Dushera) and Tihar (Deewali) festivals as a social tradition. The national card game of Nepal.

setup.deck: Three standard 52-card decks shuffled together. No printed jokers - wild cards are created during play.
setup.dealing: Each player receives 21 cards. Remaining cards form the stock. Turn to deal passes to the left (or right in some regions).

rules.objective: Form valid combinations to complete your hand and score points. Be the first to finish with a valid hand.
rules.gameplay: Standard Rummy mechanics: Draw from stock or take discard, then discard. After seeing the joker, can use wild cards in combinations. Must maintain 21 cards (draw then discard).
keyRules: Draw one card from stock or take the top discard, then discard one. Only the latest discard may be taken. Cannot discard the same card just picked from discard.

First to lay three tunnelas or pure sequences selects or sees the tiplu; that card and its poplu, jhiplu and same-rank in other suits are wild. After seeing the tiplu, may not take a joker from the discard pile.
Win by laying four more combinations and discarding last card, or by laying eight dublees (no jokers in dublees).

strategy.basic: Focus on 'seeing the joker' as fast as possible by forming three pure sets. Don't hoard high cards early - use your 21-card hand to find the easiest 3-card combinations first.
strategy.intermediate: Hand flexibility: Because you have three decks, the probability of finding a second '7 of Hearts' is high. Prioritize building 'Trials' (three identical cards) over 'Sequences' if you start with several duplicates. Track which Tiplus have been played or discarded.
strategy.advanced: Marriage Hunting: If you hold a Poplu and a Jhiplu, watch for discarded Tiplus from opponents. Since they might not realize you're building the 'Marriage', they might discard it. Calculate the probability of completing a Marriage vs. finishing quickly with a regular hand.
tips: Count the Tiplus - since there are three decks, there are three Tiplus in total
Knowing how many Tiplus are visible helps calculate your 'Marriage' potential
If you haven't 'seen' the joker yet and an opponent finishes, you pay double penalty
Pure sequences are safer than dirty sequences - prioritize them early
The Marriage bonus can be huge - sometimes worth pursuing even if it slows you down

draw.description: Take either the top card of the face-down stock or the face-up card discarded by the previous player. First player may take the card turned up by the dealer.
draw.constraints: One draw per turn. If taking from discard, only the latest discard may be taken. After seeing the tiplu, may not take a joker from the discard pile.

discard.description: Discard one card face up onto the discard pile. Must discard after drawing. A player who took the face-up card from the discard pile may not discard that same card.
discard.constraints: Exactly one discard per turn after drawing.

pass.reason: This game has no pass action.

bid.reason: This game has no bid action.

meld.description: Lay down three-card combinations: tunnela (three identical), pure sequence (three consecutive same suit), dirty sequence or triplet with jokers. First player to lay three tunnelas or pure sequences selects or sees the tiplu (wild card). Combinations are kept in hand until play ends except tunnelas at deal and the three used to see the tiplu.
meld.constraints: Must have three tunnelas or pure sequences to see the tiplu. After that, jokers (tiplu, poplu, jhiplu, ordinary jokers) may be used in combinations.

go_out.description: End the play by either laying down four more valid three-card combinations after the initial three and discarding the last card, or by laying down eight dublees (pairs of identical cards).
go_out.constraints: Legal only when hand can be fully laid out: seven combinations plus one discard, or eight dublees. Dublees may not use jokers.

engine.deckDescription: Three standard 52-card French packs shuffled together (156 cards total). No printed jokers; wild cards are created each deal when the first player to lay three tunnelas or pure sequences draws a card from the stock to become the tiplu. That card and the poplu (rank above), jhiplu (rank below), and same-rank in other suits are wild (maal).
engine.suitDescription: Suits and ranks are as defined in the deck description above; no separate suit or rank set is used for this game.

scoring.description: Points for maal (tiplu, poplu, jhiplu), marriage (jhiplu-tiplu-poplu sequence), and tunnelas exposed at deal. Winner receives 3 from each opponent who saw the joker, 10 from each who did not; plus 5 each if winner went out with eight dublees. Then each player pays others the difference in their card points (streamlined: net payment to or from the winner).
scoring.winCondition: First to lay seven three-card combinations (three to see the tiplu, then four more) and discard the last card; or first to lay eight dublees (pairs of identical cards).
